old_caption: The video captures a serene landscape scene at sunset. The sky is painted with hues of orange, pink, and blue, transitioning into darker shades as it meets the horizon. Clouds are scattered across the sky, adding depth to the scene. Below, a calm body of water reflects the vibrant colors of the sky and the silhouettes of the trees on its far bank. The trees, mostly coniferous, stand tall and dark against the colorful backdrop, their reflections shimmering on the water's surface. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, allowing viewers to take in the tranquil beauty of the scene. There are no visible animals or characters in the video, emphasizing the peaceful solitude of nature. The overall atmosphere is one of quiet contemplation, inviting viewers to appreciate the natural world.

caption: The video captures a wide, fixed landscape of a calm, partially frozen lake under a layered blue-grey sky with an orange horizon band. On the right, dark leafless trees, including one tall conifer, stand fronted by pale pinkish dry reeds. The lower half mirrors the sky, the orange glow, and the inverted trees. This mirror image is not static: the reflected tree shapes and cloud and orange bands shift, stretch, and break slightly with gentle ripples. The reflected conifer tip and the vertical streaks of the tree reflection change form and length, while the real trees stay fixed. No person, animal, or vehicle enters, and the shoreline and horizon hold their positions. The overhead clouds show little visible change, so the clearest movement is the water's. The rippling reflection is already underway and continues.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
